Recently
I completed a
two-year term as Presi
dent of the Executive Coun
cil and started a second
term in the fine tradition of
Psi U Presidents, who seem
to serve forever. However,
I won't follow in the
footsteps of some of my
predecessors, for this will
be my last term.
As I began planning for
the next two years, I posed
the question I have been as
king ever since I was
elected to the Executive
Council in 1974: "WHY
DO I STAY INVOLVED
WITH MY FRATERNITY
AFTER ALL THESE
YEARS?"
Some of my fellow
lawyers in Atlanta think it's
because my social develop
ment ended at age 22 and
that I just want to continue
the fun and games of my
fraternity days. Others
smugly conclude that I'm
just plain crazy. Of course,
neither is correct.
While I remember my
fraternity experience well, I
know that fraternity life
today is far different from
what it was in the late 60' s
and early 70' s, and that our
undergraduates are faced
with many issues and pres
sures today which my
brothers and I at

Washington & Lee Univer
sity could not have im
agined. Nevertheless, my
experience and my
knowledge is very impor
tant to the Fraternity and
SO IS YOURS! Your
fraternity experience
helped prepare you for vir
tually every endeavor you
have undertaken since you
graduated. Your total ex
perience makes you a valu
able resource to your local
alumni association, to your
chapter, and to the Interna
tional Fraternity. Volun
teers are needed to serve
as alumni association of
ficers, chapter advisors,
committee members, Foun
dation Directors, and Ex
ecutive Council members.
Upsilon establish a per
manent headquarters. The
recent bequests highlight
the wonderful opportunity
alumni have, through
planned giving, to leave a
legacy for Psi Upsilon. The
Psi Upsilon Foundation,
Inc., which is a tax exempt
under Section 501 (c)(3) of
the Internal Revenue
Code, provides a wonder
ful vehicle for estate plan
ning and is a worthwhile
repository for charitable
giving. The Foundation
supports a wide variety of
educational activities,
through scholarships and
grants for leadership
development, leadership
training, and educational
programs.
Psi Upsilon is a strong fraternity and
you, the involved, committed brothers,
continue to make it so. As I visit
chapters around the country, and see the
things, both good and bad, which affect
our undergraduates, I am constantly
heartened by the role that the alumni
play.
While our under
graduates could muddle
along without our help, or
our interference, the health
and well being of our
Fraternity depends in large
measure on your support.
Recently, Psi Upsilon
received two significant be
quests. Both were given
directly to the Fraternity
and will be used to help Psi
Psi Upsilon has existed
for 160 years because its
alumni have been loyal and
generous and willing to
give of their time, talent,
and money to aid the
Fraternity.
If Psi Upsilon is to sur
vive for another 160 years,
it must have continued
alumni involvement, both
financially and as volun
teers at all levels.

stantly heartened by the

Many of our chapters know , ,�

cial support from their

cause so many wonderful,
successful brothers give so

has been said that music soothes the savage
breast. Psi Upsilon, then, has been spared from
"savagery," for throughout her 160 year history,
music has played an in
tegral part in Psi Upsilon
occasions. Since the days
before radio, television,
and even electricity, Psi
Upsilon members have
been singing songs to enter
tain themselves and their
guests. More importantly,
the songs of the Fraternity
provide us with a different
perspective on the mean
ing of Psi Upsilon. The
chapter meeting Ritual,
dinner, and many social
functions necessitate
rounds of Psi U song, which often set the tone for
the affair. A highlight of the annual Psi Upsilon
Convention is the opportunity for delegates to
sing familiar tunes as well as learn new ones. And
a universal component of chapter member educa-

tion programs has been the recitation of verses to
old familiar tunes such as "The Psi Upsilon Smok
ing Song," "Dear Old Shrine," "Welcome Brothers,
Old & Young," and 'The Rho Owl Song." But
what about the origin of some of our most popular
songs?
The college fraternity deserves the credit for
introducing singing to American campuses. While
few college songs were written before 1850, the
first published edition of Psi Upsilon Songs dates
to 1849. Brother Francis Miles Finch, Beta '49,
began penning the first Psi Upsilon songs in 1847,
including the "Psi Upsilon Smoking Song," which
were subsequently included in the 1849 inaugural
edition of Psi Upsilon Songs.
The
familiar "Psi Upsilon SmokingSong" was
immediately hailed by critics not only for its
outstanding poetic value, but also for the literary
brilliance originated by an American college stu
dent. It has been called "the most striking poeni in
English literature which the theme of tobacco has
inspired." From the April 23, 1879 issue of 'The
Hartford Coufant":

...During one of the author's last years at
Yale, it chanced that the members of his
college society, the Psi Upsilon, were
sitting
in their chapter-room, engaged in smoking,
chatting, and singing student-songs. In an
interval of comparative silence a member
suddenly remarked, 'We've lots of drinking
songs; why don't somebody write a smoking
song?' Mr. Finch, whose facility at versifica
tion has always been remarkable, at once
withdrew into a quiet corner, and in a few
minutes produced the first three verses of
'The Smoking Song'...These were at once
sung with immense delight...The subsequent
history of the song is equally notable. It has
been published both in English and Califor
nia journals..."
Dear
Old Shrine," written by Professor Calvin
S. Harrington, Xi 1852, for the 25th anniver
sary of the Xi in 1 868, early attained a unique
place in the hearts of all Psi U 's. It has long been
the custom to sing it as a parting song in the
regulai" ritual of chapter meetings, and it is heard
again and again at reunion meetings of the chap
ters and fraternity in general. Perhaps one of the
most memorable and stirring displays of our
brotherhood occurs during the closing banquet at
the Convention when brothers link fingers to sing
"Dear Old Shrine," symbolic of the Fraternity's
close of one year and commencement of the next.

Let
us loud our voices ring, and each brother
gladly sing ..." resounds loudly throughout the
Psi Upsilon world. Brother Charles Henry Arndt,
Iota 1889, introduced 'Welcome Brothers, Old
and Young" at the 1888 Convention hosted by the
Iota. A universally known and favorite song
among members, the lyrics speak to under
graduates and alumni alike about their lifelong
commitment to the Fraternity and the Fraternity's
commitment to them.
Always sung with an unwaning enthusiasm,
though the special events which it celebrates
have become ancient history, is the "Rho Owl
Song,"by Charles Floyd McClure, Rho 1895. The
allegorical significance of what might seem to the
casual reader more or less unintelligible in this
song was explained by Brother Charles H. Ber
nard, Rho 1895, in the Pi Garnet of February 1939:
"Hurt by the decision of the Wisconsin chap
ter to sun-ender its charter and petition for
membership in Psi Upsilon, the Phi Kappa
Psi Fraternity and similar organizations,
termed by the Phi Chapter at the University
of Michigan as 'small fry societies,' at
tempted to influence existing chapters of Psi
U to refuse the Wisconsin petitioners a
charter...In the Rho Owl song, the owl 'who
dwelt in great exclusiveness' represents Psi
Upsilon, and the 'lion bold who rampant
awoke (rose) one morn awakening conster
nation in the land where he was born' is the
Wisconsin chapter which renounced Phi
Kappa Psi to seek admission into Psi Up
silon. Phi Kappa Psi and others are the
'envious jackals' who asked Psi Upsilon to
'bar from out thy portals fair this traitor
double-dyed.'"
As the 20 century ends and the 2 1 st century ap
proaches, with their many technological "distrac
tions," Psi U verse will become increasingly
important in reminding our members of the great
legacy of song and poetry provided by the
Fraternity's early members. As Brother Finch so
aptly put it in the "Psi Upsilon Anthem,"
"Until the sands of life are run, we'll sing to
thee, PSI UPSILON."

The Past is Prologue
1 00 Years Ago...
In
the Fraternity's sixtieth year, the Zeta Chapter at
Dartmouth hosted the annual Convention. Petitions for
charters were received from Alpha Zeta Phi at Dickinson
College, the order of Rho Kappa Upsilon at the University
of Wisconsin, and Phi Beta Epsilon at MIT. While Rho
Kappa Upsilon was established as the Fraternity's Rho
Chapter, the Dickinson group was rejected because the
college's endowment and enrollment were considered in
adequate; the MIT group was rejected because the In
stitute was an "exclusively technical" school.
75 Years Ago...
World
War I greatly hindered Psi Upsilon's operations.
A special Convention was held at the Waldorf-Astoria
in New York and the following, General Resolution No. 1 ,
was adopted: RESOLVED, That this Convention, in com
pliance with the known desires of the War Department,
feels that this Fraternity can best help to win the war by
suspending the functions and meetings of a social or
ceremonial nature of the Chapters for the period of the
present emergency in institutions where units of the
Students' Army Training Corps are established, which in
clude all colleges where there are Chapters of Psi Upsilon.
50 Years Ago...
The Epsilon Nu Chapter at Michigan State was officially
welcomed at the Convention which was held in Rye,
New York on June 19, 1943. Owing to the WWII, the con
ditions of Chapters were dire. The Lambda Chapter at
Columbia reported that "all undergraduates have entered
the armed services. The Chapter's quarters have been
taken over by the University and its overhead ceased..."
25 Years Ago...
The Kappa Chapter hosted the 1 26th Convention in
Brunswick, Maine. In September, over one hundred
members and guests gathered to christen the site of the
Epsilon Omega Chapter House. Speaking at the Xi
Chapter's 125th Anniversary Banquet, Edward D.
Ethenngton, President of Wesleyan University, lauded the
participation of Psi Upsilon alumni as trustees on the Wes
leyan Board. He encouraged Psi Upsilon members to
"continue to lead the way if fraternities are to maintain
their existence on Wesleyan's campus."
10 Years Ago...
Psi Upsilon celebrated its sesquicentennial anniversary
and appropriately, the Convention was hosted by the
Theta Chapter. In honor of its 1 50th anniversary, the
Fraternity presented Union College with a pyramidshaped geological timetable. Frank Duel, Mayor of
Schenectady, issued a proclamation declaring the week
of August 22-28, 1 983 "Psi Upsilon Week in the City of
Schenectady." The winter issue of The DIAMOND in
cluded a history of the Theta Chapter to 1 900.
